aboutPreview.title: A consultancy built around the research process, not around deadlines
body: SetuVidya Consultancy works with scholars and students who are navigating complex academic requirements: a doctoral committee that wants the methodology tightened, a journal that has returned a manuscript for major revision, a monograph that has been sitting unfinished for two years, an admission cycle with rules that change by university.

We provide structure. A scoped plan, a named point of contact, written feedback you can act on, and revisions until the work is ready. What we do not provide is authorship. You remain the researcher, the author and the person who submits.

sections.heading: What we do
body: SetuVidya Consultancy supports PhD scholars, M.Tech and Master's students, research scholars, faculty members, academicians, authors and applicants to university programmes.

The work covers research guidance, thesis support, publication assistance, academic writing and editing, book publication and university admission guidance. Some scholars come to us at the proposal stage and stay through to their defence. Others arrive with a single problem: a reviewer's comment they cannot answer, a chapter that will not hold together, a similarity report that needs interpreting.

sections.heading: How we position ourselves
body: We describe SetuVidya as a bridge, because that is genuinely the shape of the service. On one side sits research: questions, data, method, evidence. On the other sit the outcomes research is supposed to reach, namely knowledge that is properly recorded, publications that survive peer review, books that get read, and academic opportunities that open up as a result.

Most scholars do not fail on the research. They lose time on the crossing, on formatting rules, journal conventions, methodological justification, statistical choices, and the administrative machinery of universities. That crossing is what we are for.

sections.heading: How we work
body: Every engagement starts with an honest assessment. If your manuscript is not ready for the journal you have in mind, we say so. If your methodology will not survive a viva, we say so before you invest another six months in it.
Scope is agreed in writing before work begins. You get a named point of contact, staged deliverables and written feedback you can act on. Revisions are part of the engagement, not an upsell.

sections.heading: Where we draw the line
body: We do not sell authorship, guaranteed publication or guaranteed admission, and we do not accept work that asks us to fabricate data, manufacture citations or write something you intend to pass off as unaided.

This is not a disclaimer bolted onto the end of the service. It is the reason the service is worth buying: guidance that improves your capability is the only kind that survives a viva, a reviewer or a career.

anatomy.title: Understanding Your Thesis
anatomy.subtitle: Understand the key stages of a structured research project—from research problem to final references.

chapters.title: Introduction
body: The introduction establishes what the study is about and why it is worth doing. It moves from the broad background and context of the field down to the specific problem your work addresses.
By the end of it a reader should know exactly what gap you identified, what you set out to do about it, and how far the study extends.
points: Background and context of the study
Statement of the research problem
Significance and justification of the study
The research gap the study addresses
Research objectives
Research questions, and hypotheses where the design calls for them
Scope and delimitations of the study

chapters.title: Literature Review
body: The literature review systematically examines and synthesises previous research related to your topic. It is an argument, not a catalogue: the point is to show what is already established, where accounts disagree, and what remains unanswered.
Done well, it identifies the important theories and findings in the field and builds the foundation on which your own study stands, making the research gap unavoidable rather than asserted.
chapters.label: LOR
points: A search strategy and the databases consulted
Inclusion and exclusion criteria for the studies reviewed
Key theories and theoretical frameworks in the field
Thematic synthesis of prior findings, including contradictions
The research gap, stated explicitly
A conceptual framework linking the review to your objectives

chapters.title: Research Methodology
body: The methodology explains how the study was carried out, in enough detail that another researcher could follow the same route. It is the section examiners scrutinise most closely, because every later claim depends on it.
What it contains varies by discipline. A survey-based management study, a laboratory-based science study and an archival humanities study will each justify very different choices.
points: Research design and the rationale for it
Research approach: quantitative, qualitative or mixed methods
Population, sample and sampling technique
Variables and their operational definitions, where applicable
Data sources, primary or secondary
Research instruments, and their validity and reliability
Data collection procedure and ethical considerations
Methods of analysis, matched to the data and the hypotheses
chapters.toolsLabel: Tools that may be appropriate, depending on the design

chapters.title: Results & Analysis
body: This section presents and analyses what the data actually showed. Results are reported here; their meaning is argued in the discussion that follows.
The techniques below are illustrative. Which of them belong in your thesis follows entirely from your research design, your data and your discipline.
chapters.pointsLabel: Examples of analysis, depending on the design
points: Descriptive statistics
Reliability and validity analysis
Correlation analysis
Regression analysis
Hypothesis testing
Factor analysis
Structural equation modelling (SEM / PLS-SEM)
Tables and figures prepared to the required format
Qualitative coding and thematic analysis
chapters.note: Not every method applies to every subject. A qualitative study in literature or history may use none of the statistical techniques listed here.

chapters.title: Discussion
body: The discussion interprets the findings and connects them back to the research objectives, to the theories you drew on, and to the previous studies reviewed earlier.
Its job is explanation, not repetition. A discussion that restates the results table has not done the work; one that explains why a finding agrees with some prior studies and contradicts others has.
points: Interpretation of each major finding against the objectives
Agreement and disagreement with previous studies, and why
How the findings sit with the theoretical framework
Theoretical and practical implications
Unexpected results, addressed rather than omitted

chapters.title: Conclusion
body: The conclusion draws the study together: what was found, what it contributes, and what it does not settle. It should be readable on its own by someone who has read only the introduction.
points: A summary of the major findings
The overall contribution of the study to the field
Theoretical, practical or policy implications
Limitations, stated honestly
Suggestions for future research

chapters.title: References — APA 7th Edition
body: References document every source cited in the study, and must be complete, consistent and correctly styled. Where your institution requires APA 7th Edition, the patterns below apply.
These are formatting templates, not real publications. Replace each placeholder with the details of the source you are actually citing.
points: Every in-text citation has a matching reference, and vice versa
Alphabetical ordering by author surname
Hanging indent and consistent punctuation
Journal titles and volumes in italics, as APA requires
DOIs given as full https://doi.org/ links
Confirm the edition your university requires before formatting

Thesis consultancy.q: Will you write my thesis for me?
Thesis consultancy.a: We provide guidance, structural review, methodology support, analysis, editing and formatting throughout the research process. The research and final writing remain your responsibility, so that the work you submit accurately represents your own academic work.

Thesis consultancy.q: At what stage should I approach you?
Thesis consultancy.a: Any stage. Earlier is generally cheaper and less painful, because problems with scope and methodology are far more expensive to fix after data has been collected. That said, a large share of our work is with scholars responding to committee revisions late in the process.

Thesis consultancy.q: Can you help if my supervisor has already rejected a draft?
Thesis consultancy.a: Yes. Send us the draft and the feedback. We work backwards from the specific objections rather than starting over, and we will tell you if we think the feedback points to a deeper structural problem.

Thesis consultancy.q: Do you work to my university's specific format?
Thesis consultancy.a: Yes. Send us the thesis handbook or template and we work to it, including margins, citation style, chapter numbering, table and figure conventions and front matter.
Yes, without exception. Drafts, data and identities are never reused, shown to other clients, or published as samples.

Research publication.q: Can you guarantee my paper will be published?
Research publication.a: Publication decisions are made by journal editors and peer reviewers. We support manuscript improvement, journal selection, author-guideline compliance and submission preparation, while the final publication decision remains with the journal.

Research publication.q: How do you choose which journal to target?
Research publication.a: By reading your manuscript against what the journal has actually published recently, not against its stated scope alone. We check current indexing status, typical review timelines where published, article-processing charges and the fit of your contribution to the readership.

Research publication.q: What happens if reviewers ask for major revisions?
Research publication.a: That is a normal and often good outcome. We help you build a point-by-point response that addresses each comment with evidence, identifies exactly where the manuscript changed, and disagrees respectfully where a comment is mistaken.

Research publication.q: Do you charge for publication or pay journals?
Research publication.a: Never. We charge for our editorial and advisory work only. We do not pay journals, broker acceptance or use any channel that bypasses peer review. Any article-processing charge is paid by you, directly to the journal.

Research publication.q: Can you add me as an author to an existing paper?
Research publication.a: No. Authorship sale is research misconduct and we do not participate in it in any form.

SCI & Scopus.q: What is the difference between SCI, SCIE and Scopus?
SCI & Scopus.a: SCI and its expanded form SCIE are citation indexes maintained by Clarivate within the Web of Science. Scopus is a separate abstract and citation database maintained by Elsevier. They have different coverage, different inclusion criteria and different metrics. A journal may be in one, both or neither.

SCI & Scopus.q: How do I know a journal is genuinely indexed?
SCI & Scopus.a: Check the source lists published by Clarivate and Elsevier directly, not the journal's own website. Indexing can be discontinued, and delisted journals often continue advertising former status. We verify this as part of journal selection.

SCI & Scopus.q: How long does review take at an indexed journal?
SCI & Scopus.a: It varies enormously, from a few weeks to well over a year. Where a journal publishes its median times we will tell you; where it does not, we can only give you a range based on the field.

SCI & Scopus.q: Is a high-impact journal always the right target?
SCI & Scopus.a: No. Submitting to a journal well above the level of your contribution usually costs months for a desk rejection. We aim for the strongest journal your work can realistically support, which is a different question.

Peer-reviewed journals.q: How do I avoid predatory journals?
Peer-reviewed journals.a: Warning signs include unsolicited invitations, promises of publication within days, unclear or hidden fees, editorial boards that cannot be verified, and claimed indexing you cannot confirm at the source. We screen candidate journals for these as standard.

It depends on your institution's requirement. Check your university's specific criteria, since some require indexed publication specifically. We will read the requirement with you before targeting anything.

Peer-reviewed journals.q: Can you help with conference papers?
Peer-reviewed journals.a: Yes, including selection of credible conferences, formatting to the proceedings template, and preparation of presentation material.

Book publication.q: Can I turn my thesis into a book?
Book publication.a: Often, but not by reprinting it. A thesis is written to demonstrate competence to examiners; a book is written to be read. That usually means cutting the methodological apparatus, rewriting the literature review as context, and rebuilding the argument for a reader who is not obliged to finish it. We advise on the restructuring.

Book publication.q: Do you publish the book yourself?
Book publication.a: No. We provide editorial, design and production support, and we explain publisher options. You choose and contract directly with your publisher or platform, so the rights and the relationship stay with you.

An ISBN identifies a specific edition and format of a title. Each format needs its own. Who registers it depends on your publishing route, and it affects who is recorded as publisher. We explain the implications before you commit.

Book publication.q: What does an edited volume involve?
Book publication.a: Coordinating contributors, setting and enforcing a chapter template, reviewing submissions for quality and consistency, chasing deadlines, and building coherent front and back matter. We can support any or all of that.

University admission.a: Admission decisions are made by universities. We help you identify suitable programmes, understand eligibility requirements and prepare a complete, accurate and well-organised application. The final admission decision remains with the university.

University admission.q: Will you write my statement of purpose?
University admission.a: No. We advise on structure, focus and clarity, and give feedback on your drafts. The content and the words must be yours. Universities increasingly screen for this, and a generic or purchased statement is easy to spot.

University admission.q: Are you affiliated with any universities?
University admission.a: No. We hold no agency arrangements, commissions or partnerships with institutions, which is what allows our shortlisting advice to be genuinely independent.
For most programmes, six to twelve months before the deadline. Documentation, attestation and entrance requirements take longer than applicants expect.

articles.title: How to read a call for papers before you submit
articles.excerpt: A call for papers tells you more than a deadline. Here is what to check before committing months of work.
articles.body:
Scope comes first. Read the last two issues the journal actually published and ask whether your paper would sit comfortably beside them.

Then the practical constraints: word limits, reference style, figure requirements, and whether the submission portal wants anonymised files.

Finally, verify the journal's indexing at the source rather than on the journal's own website.
articles.author: SetuVidya editorial
articles.seoTitle: How to read a call for papers before you submit
articles.metaDescription: A call for papers tells you more than a deadline. Here is what to check before committing months of work.

articles.title: What a research gap actually is
articles.excerpt: “Limited research exists” is an assertion. A gap is something your literature review demonstrates.
articles.body:
A gap is not an absence you assert in one sentence. It is a conclusion a reader reaches because of how you organised the evidence.

Organise the review by theme or by debate rather than by author. When the subheadings are concepts, the unanswered question tends to surface on its own.
articles.author: SetuVidya editorial
articles.seoTitle: What a research gap actually is
articles.metaDescription: “Limited research exists” is an assertion. A gap is something your literature review demonstrates.

articles.title: Choosing a postgraduate programme you can actually finish
articles.excerpt: Eligibility, supervision and funding decide more about your experience than the prospectus does.
articles.body:
Check supervision capacity in your specific area, not the department's overall reputation.

Read the regulations on registration period, extensions and submission before you apply.

Ask what happens if your supervisor leaves partway through.
articles.author: SetuVidya editorial
articles.seoTitle: Choosing a postgraduate programme you can actually finish
articles.metaDescription: Eligibility, supervision and funding decide more about your experience than the prospectus does.

articles.title: Understanding a similarity report
articles.excerpt: A similarity percentage is not a plagiarism verdict. Reading the report properly matters more than the number.
articles.body:
A high percentage can come entirely from correctly quoted material, reference lists and standard methodological phrasing.

Open the matched sources and look at what actually matched. A single uncited paragraph matters more than thirty percent spread across a bibliography.
articles.author: SetuVidya editorial
articles.metaDescription: A similarity percentage is not a plagiarism verdict. Reading the report properly matters more than the number.

articles.title: Preparing documents for a postgraduate application
articles.excerpt: Most rejected applications are incomplete rather than unqualified. A checklist approach avoids that.
articles.body:
Work backwards from the deadline and allow time for attestation, translation and transcripts, which routinely take longer than expected.

Keep one master folder with every document in the format each institution asks for, rather than converting files under time pressure.
articles.author: SetuVidya editorial
articles.seoTitle: Preparing documents for a postgraduate application
articles.metaDescription: Most rejected applications are incomplete rather than unqualified. A checklist approach avoids that.

articles.title: Writing a statement of purpose that says something
articles.excerpt: Committees read hundreds. Specificity about your research interest is what separates one from the rest.
articles.body:
Name the problem you want to work on and why it is unresolved. Name the people whose work you would build on.

Avoid biography that does not connect to the research, and avoid claiming passion in place of describing work you have actually done.
articles.author: SetuVidya editorial
articles.seoTitle: Writing a statement of purpose that says something
articles.metaDescription: Committees read hundreds. Specificity about your research interest is what separates one from the rest.

articles.title: What peer review actually involves
articles.excerpt: Understanding the stages makes reviewer comments far less alarming when they arrive.
articles.body:
Desk screening comes first, and most rejections happen here on scope rather than quality.

Reviewers are asked whether the method supports the claims. Major revisions are a normal, often positive outcome, not a failure.
